structured.approach:
I followed the design-steps skill for DES-02. First I read all six contracted inputs: the PRD, prototype, TRD, org.architecture, org.data_model and org.design_library. I also read the approved stories (via context_get), the DES-01 check record, the requirement file and the code in the step's tool view. The approved TRD already fixes the interfaces (IF-1 to IF-8, CT-1), so the design builds on it rather than re-deriving it.

The HLD covers context, components, the inter-repository data contracts (DC-1 to DC-4 and CT-1), data flow, non-functional needs, security and tenancy, and design decisions DD-1 to DD-11, each citing its source.

The LLD covers each repository: modules, function signatures, algorithms, data structures, error handling, and tests mapped to TRD tests T-1 to T-17 and story criteria. Build tasks name their components, tests and size.

I promoted the approved low-fidelity wireframes to feat.screens. It holds the exact HTML for each state, annotated frames, copy, accessibility notes and a check against the prototype and PRD. org.design_library says Figma is not connected and no Figma connector is approved, so I filed a capability request for one and delivered the screens in text form.

Coding plan: no lane imports another lane's code, and each lane builds against a documented data contract, so all four lanes run in one parallel stage.

A verifier subagent checked both outputs against the inputs and code. I applied its fixes: a dangling reference, a contradiction in empty-rows handling, unlabelled design choices, story ID citations, a sequence-diagram arrow, the source of the DL numbering, and the external dependencies.

claims.text: The design keeps the four-repository topology and the runtimes, Python 3.9 for ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging and Node.js 22 CommonJS for ap_portal, and introduces no new technology.

Every change is either a new function or an additive extension of an existing one, as the rule "Keep every existing signature; add new functions" requires. The only existing functions touched are to_model, which gains paid_date handling, and build_explanation_request, which gains risk=None as its last parameter.
The Invoice record gains paid_date (date or None), which was added in feed v3. The record stays a plain dict, because the code has no Invoice class.

The design adopts CT-1 as the ap_aging to ap_portal contract: a JSON array of objects with id, vendor, days (integer), amount (two-decimal string) and risk. ap_aging owns serialisation through overdue_rows_to_json. Confirmation of CT-1 (TQ-3) is still open.
overdue_with_risk lists unpaid invoices only when days past due is greater than 30 and never calls bucket_for. This matters because bucket_for returns "31-60" for exactly 30 days.

Amounts stay Decimal in Python, are quantised with Decimal("0.01"), and are carried as strings in JSON and in ap_portal. renderOverdueRisk never uses formatAmount, because formatAmount converts through Number(...).toFixed(2).
vendor_risk returns 'high' when predict_delay_days(history) > 30, 'medium' when it is > 10, and 'low' otherwise. It makes no LLM call.

The screen applies the design-library rules exactly: class 'overdue-risk', the row classes risk-high, risk-medium, risk-low and risk-unknown, the columns Invoice, Vendor, Days overdue and Amount, and nothing rendered when there are no rows. The library defines no tokens, so the screen applies none.

The populated frame uses the prototype's synthetic rows in this order: SYN-INV-004 (75 days, 1250.00, high), SYN-INV-002 (42, 980.50, medium), SYN-INV-003 (42, 15.00, unknown), SYN-INV-001 (31, 300.00, low).
Figma is not connected, so the final screens are delivered in text form. A Figma MCP connector was requested in this step.
DES-01 found no platform-level change. This design adds no transport, storage, provider change or deployed harness, any of which would re-trigger DES-01.

Within a lane, the delay-history story depends on the paid_date story and the serialiser story depends on the overdue-list story. The portal story depends only on the CT-1 contract, so it can be built in parallel.

Coding lanes map one to one to repositories: ap_pipeline to Data Engineering, ap_forecast to Data Science, ap_aging to Backend and ap_portal to Frontend. The end-to-end test belongs to the Testing Agent, not to a coding lane.
Every lane must keep CI green: compile, unit tests, coverage of at least 90%, and static checks.
Coding plan: DE + DS + BE + FE. No lane imports another lane's code; each builds against a documented data contract (DC-1 to DC-3, CT-1).

open_questions: DQ-1: No input names the production component that calls the stages in sequence and carries CT-1 from ap_aging to ap_portal. The design adds no transport; the end-to-end harness is the only wiring. Adding a transport would re-trigger DES-01.
DQ-2: Which rounding mode applies when a malformed feed amount has more than two decimals? The design assumes the default decimal context (round-half-even).
DQ-3: Should ap_portal throw TypeError on a CT-1 violation (non-array rows, non-string amount, non-integer days), as the design proposes, or render a fallback?
DQ-4: Should delays_by_vendor be re-exported from ap_pipeline/__init__.py? The package has no __all__ today.
DQ-5: Approve the requested Figma MCP connector so the screens can be published as Figma frames (same request as prototype question PQ-P6).

Carried, with interim answers in the design: TQ-1 to TQ-11 from the TRD (notably TQ-3 on CT-1 approval, TQ-8 on sending the risk label to the provider, TQ-10, TQ-11), OQ-B1 to OQ-B10 and PQ-1 to PQ-6 from the PRD, PQ-P1 to PQ-P7 from the prototype, and SQ-1 to SQ-4 from the stories.
structured.summary:
I wrote feat.design (HLD and LLD) and feat.screens for FEAT-ZD-48600, as drafts for the Architect and UX lead gate.

**feat.design, HLD:**
- 10 components across the four repositories and the test harness.
- The data contracts between repositories: DC-1 to DC-4 and the CT-1 JSON contract.
- A data-flow sequence, non-functional needs, security and tenancy (no tenancy surface, tier T2).
- 11 cited design decisions.

**feat.design, LLD for each repository:**
- Modules, signatures and algorithms.
- Data structures, error handling, and tests mapped to the TRD tests and story criteria.

**Build tasks:** DT-1 to DT-7, each naming its components, tests and size.

**Coding plan:** all four lanes run in parallel (DE + DS + BE + FE), because they share only documented data contracts.

**feat.screens:** promotes the approved wireframes to an exact screen specification: the exact HTML for the populated and empty states, defensive states, copy, accessibility notes and a check against the prototype and PRD. Figma is not connected, so I requested a Figma connector and delivered the screens in text form.

A verifier pass found no wrong IDs, code facts or markup; I applied its fixes for wording and labelling. There are no blocking questions.

tool_input.description: Check the design ends with one coding-plan line
